Thanks for the call this morning. Our security and cloud teams asked me to confirm a couple of items before we finalize the MAP and commit the POC window: 

- We need a clear list of what credentials you will provision versus what Beacon must create (API keys, service accounts, role bindings).

Susan — thanks for the quick follow. I pulled together a focused MAP slice that targets the environment gating items you called out. Attaching a single-page MAP extract + three technical artifacts (vpc peering template, ip allowlist template, and a short credentialing playbook). Key points below and an explicit 10 business-day close runway we believe is realistic for a POC start.

High-level ownership and deliverables (summary):
- Redwood (owner: Vivek / neha)
  - Provision test API keys scoped to Beacon evaluation org (read/generate tokens) — Redwood creates keys and shares via secure link (expected T+1 business day).
  - Provide vpc-peering-template.yaml and peering acceptance checklist (attached).
  - Provide IP ingress ranges we will advertise for the dedicated inference cluster (stable /24 blocks per region).
- Beacon (owner: Susan / platform-ops)
  - Create evaluation org and invite Redwood service account (we will provide principal name).
  - Apply CIDR ranges to your routing policies and create peering connection.
  - Add Redwood ingress IPs to allowlist and confirm egress NAT if required.

Timeline (working cadence):
1) Day 0: MAP sign and ticket open in your tracker (we prefer a simple SOW-lite via DocuSign link; I included HubSpot deal id in the doc).
2) Day 1–2: Redwood issues evaluation API keys, service account principal, and share peering template + ip-allowlist CSV.
3) Day 3–6: Beacon infra implements peering and allowlist; provides peering connection id and test endpoints.
4) Day 7–10: Joint smoke tests, token-based auth checks, and perf baseline (short runbook included).

Technical notes (short):
- Peering type: we support both direct VPC peering and transit gateway; for production we recommend a dedicated peering for isolation. For the evaluation window, a transit/shared peer is acceptable if you can guarantee path stability.
- IP ranges: Redwood will publish stable /24s per region. For this POC we can reserve a single /24 in us-west-2; if you need smaller ranges we can coordinate NAT egress mapping.
- Keys: API keys are short-lived (90 days) for eval; we will rotate on request. We also support scoped service principals if Beacon prefers token exchange via your KMS.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_MAP_v1.2.pdf — MAP extract with milestones and acceptance criteria.
- vpc-peering-template.yaml — sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet your infra can drop into the runbook.
- ip-allowlist-template.csv — CSV you can paste into firewall/ACL consoles.

Next step: I propose a 30-minute technical alignment tomorrow at 10am PT with your platform-ops engineer so we can hand off the peering template and confirm the CIDR. Is that workable?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni

Hi Susan / platform team — looping in the infra detail so you get exactly what to hand to your network engineers. A few implementation clarifications from the runtime/ops side: 

- Peering template: the attached YAML includes both the peering resource and the route table changes required for our inference subnet. If you use Terraform, the resource names are annotated as comments.
- Required details from Beacon: (a) the exact CIDR you plan to expose to Redwood (we need a routable /24 or an agreed NAT translation table), (b) the account ID and preferred endpoint hostname to attach for TLS SAN validation, (c) an infra contact with permissions to accept peering connections.
- IP allowlist behaviour: our ingress IPs are static for the reserved eval cluster. They will not change during the 10-day window; we will give you the exact list when keys are issued. For longer pilots / prod we supply a signed SAML assertion or can integrate via your KMS.

Security checklist highlights (quick):
- Keys shared via pre-signed secure link (expires 72 hours).
- Audit logs: we will enable token-level logging for the POC; you can request a retention window for these artifacts.
- Data handling: Redwood processes request tokens for inference and does not persist customer payloads beyond cache TTL unless explicitly enabled. The MAP includes a line item to confirm this behaviour for compliance.

I attached the little ip-allowlist-template.csv you can paste into your firewall UI. If you can share the initial peering request id and the infra contact I will ping our peering ops to accept within 24 hours.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
